categories.landscape:
Searches: Hub listings by downloads, newest and trending for the sentence-similarity and feature-extraction pipelines; name searches for every family in the brief; org listings (Qwen, google, nvidia, microsoft, ibm-granite, perplexity-ai, MongoDB, jinaai, Snowflake, Alibaba-NLP, BAAI, nomic-ai, mixedbread-ai, tencent, codefuse-ai, Octen, KaLM-Embedding, lightonai, LiquidAI, NeuML, zeroentropy, TencentBAC); HF papers. Standings were computed myself from a sparse clone of github.com/embeddings-benchmark/results using mteb 2.26.33, not from the leaderboard UI. Coverage: complete MTEB(eng,v2) runs exist for 194 models and RTEB(Health) for 73.

Trends since mid-2025:
- Decoder LLMs converted to bidirectional encoders (Nemotron-3-Embed, pplx diffusion-pretrained Qwen3, voyage-4-nano, LFM2.5, QZhou, Giga).
- Prune-and-distill small models from large teachers (Harrier 270m/0.6b, Nemotron-3-Embed-1B, ternary bitnet-embedding).
- Native int8/binary QAT (pplx, voyage-4-nano, zembed-1).
- Shared embedding spaces across model sizes for asymmetric indexing (Voyage-4 family, pplx-embed-v2-context 0.6b/9b).
- A strong shift to multimodal (EmbeddingGemma 2, Nemotron-3.5-Embed, jina-v5-omni, Qwen3-VL-Embedding, WeMM, UEmbed, EVIE, core-emb). I excluded these except EmbeddingGemma 2; EmbeddingGemma 2 is no better on English or biology text than v1.

On health retrieval, the clearest new open leader is Nemotron-3-Embed-8B: RTEB(Health) 75.54 vs Qwen3-Embedding-8B 71.31. Its 1B distillate rivals Qwen3-8B. Harrier-27B tops MTEB(Multilingual,v2) at 74.32. BM25 still beats nearly every embedder on RTEB's EnglishHealthcare1 (68.75), which echoes the haystack finding. MTEB averages mislead for biology: F2LLM-v2 small models and QZhou rank high but are weak on TRECCOVID and SciFact. Several MTEB-eng-v2 leaders are Qwen3-Embedding fine-tunes or API-only (JCorners/Ingot-8B-R3 is proprietary, 'open_weights: false').

Looked for but did not find on the Hub:
- Any Qwen3-Embedding text successor (Qwen3.5/3.6-Embedding); Qwen only released Qwen3-VL-Embedding in 2026-01.
- jina-embeddings-v5 text base/large; only nano and small, plus omni.
- Snowflake arctic-embed v2.5/v3, new nomic or mxbai dense text models, new stella/jasper beyond Jasper-Token-Compression, a new BAAI bge dense text model (only bge-reasoner-embed, 2025-09), a new Alibaba gte text-only model (only multimodal UEmbed/core-emb/GVE), and Cohere open weights. LGAI exists only as a Mistral-7B 'Preview' reproduction.

Out of scope (other categories): reasoning-retrieval specialists (Diver-Retriever, RTriever, bge-reasoner, llama-nv-embed-reasoning), late-interaction or hybrid models (uibk-embedding-v1, pplx-embed-v2-late, LateOn), and the multilingual small models granite-embedding r2, LFM2.5-Embedding and Tarka; none showed a bio advantage.

Cost estimates scale the project's own measured L4 throughputs (results/embedding_throughput_gpu.csv) at ~350 tokens per abstract and $0.94 per L4-hour. Treat any figure for a model not in that CSV as an estimate.
categories.summary:
The finder was reliable on facts. All 19 repos exist under the stated IDs. Every metadata field (params, created, license, gated, 30-day downloads) matched the live API exactly. Every results-repo number I checked reproduced from the raw JSON with mteb 2.26.33, and a spot-check against live GitHub matched the clone. Corrections:
- Nemotron-3-Embed-1B does NOT 'match or beat' Qwen3-Embedding-8B on health. It wins only on EnglishHealthcare1 (67.19 vs 63.54) and loses on RTEB(Health) overall (67.87 vs 71.31).
- UltraBERT's 'BEIR 47.7 / GLUE 91.0' belong to the 380M encoder; the 150M base scores 45.2 / 89.5.
- voyage-4-nano does have 28 task results in the repo, none of them bio.
- The voyage-4-large 2048-d API variant (76.14) tops Nemotron-8B on RTEB(Health).
- KaLM mini needs trust_remote_code.
- Dollar figures use $0.94/L4-h; the project's own throughput CSV records $0.48.
New caveat: the suite's R2MED Biology task is the same dataset as BRIGHT Biology (identical mteb stats), and BRIGHT was a Nemotron synthetic-data seed. Priority changes: EmbeddingGemma 2 and zembed-1 drop to low. Nothing was dropped; Jasper-Token-Compression stays at low despite 0 downloads in 30 days. Outside this category, the late-interaction topk-io/topk-embed-v1-small/xsmall (2026-09-23, Apache-2.0) score 83.28/81.29 on EnglishHealthcare1, far above any single-vector model; flag them for the late-interaction survey.

candidates.name: Nemotron-3-Embed-1B
candidates.kind: dense embedder (bidirectional, mean-pooled; Ministral-3-3B pruned to 1.14B over two prune+distill rounds, distilled from Nemotron-3-Embed-8B)
candidates.license: OpenMDW-1.1 (cardData: other/openmdw-1.1; card: 'ready for commercial use')
candidates.dims_or_context: 2048-d; can be sliced to 1024/512 and re-normalised; max seq 32,768 (card evals at 4,096); 'query: ' / 'passage: ' prefixes; transformers>=5.2.0, sentence-transformers>=5.4.1; NVFP4 sibling repo (nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-NVFP4); card says FP8 works in vLLM on Hopper and Ada (L4 is Ada)
candidates.evidence: Card (seq 4096), avg nDCG@10: RTEB 72.38, ViDoRe-V3 text 57.74, MMTEB(Retrieval) 71.04. Results repo, RTEB(Health, beta) mean 67.87: ChatDoctor 68.08, CUREv1 58.12 (11 splits x en/es/fr), EnglishHealthcare1 67.19, GermanHealthcare1 78.10. Qwen3-Embedding-8B in the same repo: 71.31 / 73.22 / 60.85 / 63.54 / 87.62. So it beats Qwen3-8B only on the English health task. BM25 (mteb baseline-bm25s) EnglishHealthcare1 68.75. No MTEB(eng,v2) run. Card training data includes PubMedQA; BRIGHT is listed as a seed set for synthetic queries.
candidates.relevance: A: a 1B frontier point that beats Qwen3-Embedding-4B/8B on the English health retrieval task (EnglishHealthcare1) at roughly a sixth of the 8B's compute. Run it on the main gene-disease task, the 12-task suite and the haystack, where it tests BM25-beats-embedders (BM25 also edges it on EnglishHealthcare1). Caveat: the suite's R2MED Biology task is the same dataset as BRIGHT Biology, a Nemotron seed set, so flag that task as possibly contaminated. C/E: the most affordable credible 'large modern model' for the 7.76M geometry comparison.
candidates.cost_to_try: GPU, no trust_remote_code; needs transformers>=5.2 (Ministral3). Estimate ~12k tok/s on L4, between the project's measured Qwen3-0.6B (16.7k) and F2LLM-v2-1.7B (9.3k), at ~350 tok/abstract. 1.7M ≈ 14 L4-h (~$7 at the CSV's $0.48 spot rate, ~$13 at $0.94). 7.76M ≈ 63 L4-h (~$30 spot, ~$59 at $0.94). FP8 in vLLM on L4 may cut this further (card validated FP8 only on H100). Main task and suite: a few L4-hours.
candidates.verify_note: Metadata matches the live API exactly. Card numbers (72.38/57.74/71.04, 2048-d, 32,768, prefixes, BRIGHT seed, PubMedQA) confirmed. Results-repo numbers reproduced from raw JSON; CUREv1 58.12 is the mteb mean over all 11 splits including 'all'. Corrected the relevance claim 'matches or beats Qwen3-Embedding-8B on health retrieval': it trails Qwen3-8B on ChatDoctor (-5.1), CUREv1 (-2.7), GermanHealthcare1 (-9.5) and RTEB(Health) overall (67.87 vs 71.31), and wins only on EnglishHealthcare1 (+3.7). Added the R2MED Biology = BRIGHT Biology finding: mteb descriptive stats are identical (57,462 samples, 103 queries, 374 qrels). The successor Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B (2026-10-07) keeps this model's text LM frozen, so its text embeddings are the same; no text upgrade. High stays: it is cheap and answers the C/E model-choice question.

candidates.name: Nemotron-3-Embed-8B
candidates.kind: dense embedder (bidirectional, mean-pooled; Ministral-3-8B base); successor to the covered llama-embed-nemotron-8b
candidates.dims_or_context: 4096-d; can be sliced to 2048/1024; max seq 32,768 (card evals at 4,096); 'query: ' / 'passage: ' prefixes; FP8 in vLLM on Hopper/Ada
candidates.evidence: Card (seq 4096): RTEB-16 78.46, ViDoRe-V3 text 60.60, MMTEB(Retrieval) 75.45. Card claims #1 on multilingual RTEB as of 2026-07-16. Results repo, RTEB(Health, beta) 75.54: ChatDoctor 76.90, CUREv1 65.49, EnglishHealthcare1 71.30, GermanHealthcare1 88.48. Qwen3-Embedding-8B: 71.31 / 73.22 / 60.85 / 63.54 / 87.62. On RTEB(Health) it is the top open-weights single-vector model. The API voyage-4-large scores 75.64 at default dims and 76.14 at embed_dim=2048. Its EnglishHealthcare1 71.30 is the best single-vector score in the repo and one of only 3 models above BM25 (68.75); the other two are late-interaction topk-embed-v1 models. BRIGHT was a synthetic-data seed set. No MTEB(eng,v2) run.
candidates.relevance: A: the strongest open single-vector health retriever, and a direct challenger to Qwen3-Embedding-8B (current top embedder) on the main gene-disease task and the 12-task suite. It also re-tests 'no LLM-vs-embedder difference' against a stronger embedder. Same caveat as the 1B: the suite's R2MED Biology is the same dataset as BRIGHT Biology, a seed set. If only one Nemotron is run, run the 1B first.
candidates.cost_to_try: GPU, no trust_remote_code; fits an L4 in bf16 (~16 GB weights). At Qwen3-8B's measured 2.6k tok/s on L4: 1.7M ≈ 64 L4-h (~$31 spot, ~$60 at $0.94). 7.76M ≈ 290 L4-h (~$139 spot), over budget unless FP8 vLLM on L4 or an H100. Main task plus suite is roughly 10-30 L4-h (estimate).
candidates.verify_note: Metadata matches the live API. Card table and the 2026-07-16 RTEB claim confirmed. All four health task scores reproduced, and the EnglishHealthcare1 value matches live GitHub raw JSON. Corrected 'only voyage-4-large (75.64) is close': the voyage-4-large embed_dim=2048 entry scores 76.14, above Nemotron-8B. Added FP8 on Ada (card) and the R2MED = BRIGHT Biology contamination link. High is defensible: it is the model most likely to displace Qwen3-8B as top embedder, and testing it on the main task plus suite costs tens of dollars.

candidates.params: 268M (268,098,176); ~168M of it is the 262k-token embedding table

Queries encode on CPU; the 35M doc vectors would be re-embedded once on GPU (640-d float32 ≈ 90 GB vs ≈ 54 GB at 384-d). A: a cheap new frontier point between bge-base and Qwen3-0.6B, and a possible fine-tune base.

Bulk docs on CPU are slow: the BitNet card measures its own F16 270M GGUF at ~1.2-1.4k tok/s per 8 threads, about 190 h on the full 112-core box for 35M. On L4 (estimate; ~100M non-embedding params, about bge-base class): 1.7M ≈ 1.3-4 h, 7.76M ≈ 6-17 h, 35M ≈ 25-75 h (~$12-36 spot). No trust_remote_code.

Corrected 'base encoder 47.7 BEIR and 91.0 GLUE': those are the UltraBERT-380M row; the 150M base scores GLUE 89.5, BEIR 45.2. candidates.kind: dense embedder (open-weights member of Voyage 4; 12-layer bidirectional Qwen3-style; shares embedding space with the voyage-4/-lite/-large API models)
candidates.dims_or_context: 2048-d default, MRL 1024/512/256; context 32,000 per card (code uses max_length 32768); quantisation-aware: float32/int8/uint8/binary/ubinary; prompts 'Represent the query for retrieving supporting documents: ' / 'Represent the document for retrieval: '; GGUF repo MongoDB/voyage-4-nano-GGUF

candidates.relevance: A: a new asymmetric cost axis. Embed the 1.7M haystack or main-task docs locally with nano and encode only the queries with the voyage-4-large API, or the reverse, without re-indexing. This tests whether a cheap doc encoder plus a strong query encoder recovers most of the large model's quality.
candidates.cost_to_try: trust_remote_code. 12 layers x 1024 hidden (~190M non-embedding params), so likely faster than the finder's estimate: ~35-70k tok/s on L4 (my estimate), 1.7M ≈ 2.5-5 L4-h. Query-side API cost for 500 queries is small. CPU possible via GGUF for small sets.
candidates.verify_note: Metadata matches. Card claims (shared space, MRL dims, QAT precisions, prompts, trust_remote_code, GGUF) confirmed; context is stated as 32000. Vendor Healthcare numbers confirmed in the zembed-1 card. Corrected 'No nano runs in the repo': results/mongodb__voyage-4-nano has 28 task files, but no health or bio tasks. Lowered the cost estimate from config (12 layers, 1024 hidden, 3072 intermediate). Medium kept: the asymmetric experiment is novel for the paper, but there is no independent bio evidence.

categories.landscape:
Bio-specific dense embedders from mid-2025 to Nov 2026 fall into two groups. Small BERT/bge-base fine-tunes: BioHiCL, EDEL, NeuML's BiomedBERT line, MedTE. LoRA-tuned LLM retrievers that edge past BMRetriever by about 0.3-3 nDCG points on the BEIR biomedical subsets: REPAIR, STM. None of them compares against Qwen3-Embedding-4B/8B. The leaderboards that matter for your suite are led by general or reasoning-tuned embedders. R2MED: BGE-Reasoner first (43.18 avg), BMRetriever-7B at 30.18, MedCPT last at 9.02. BRIGHT biology: DIVER 41.8. MTEB(Medical): a Nemotron-3-Embed-8B variant claims 68.80. So the 'bio-specific vs general' gap you see probably holds.

No new releases from ncbi (MedCPT), FremyCompany (BioLORD), abhinand (MedEmbed), BMRetriever or bisectgroup (no BiCA successor), and allenai has no SPECTER3. NeuML is the only active PubMed-embedder shop (small/base/nano embedders plus ColBERT, SPLADE and cross-encoder siblings; those belong to other categories). I found no model trained for gene-disease association or literature-based discovery. The closest are EDEL (retrieval for curating KB records) and a dictyBase gene-literature benchmark (arXiv 2610.03130). That benchmark found BM25 strong and gene-synonym query expansion helpful, which matches your haystack result and is worth citing.

How I searched: Hub search across pubmed/biomed/medical/clinical/scientific/chem/gene terms, sorted by downloads, likes and createdAt, filtered by pipeline. Org listings: NeuML, ncbi, abhinand, FremyCompany, bisectgroup, BMRetriever, allenai, cambridgeltl, AQ-MedAI, EMBO, OpenMed, big labs. Bio-named derivatives of Qwen3-Embedding, embeddinggemma, bge, MedCPT, MedEmbed and PubMedBERT. The MTEB results repo. HF papers. Semantic Scholar citations of MedCPT and BMRetriever (BiCA and SapBERT were rate-limited, so not covered). The R2MED leaderboard, the BRIGHT table on the DIVER card, and BioASQ 2026 notes.

Not found: a public MedTEB leaderboard, MTEB(Medical) standings beyond one model card, any clinical-note embedder relevant to PubMed gene work (skipped), and released weights for MedEIR, NeuroMAP and QIME (QIME is 0 downloads, CC-BY-NC). Most Hub 'medical embedding' repos are student fine-tunes with no evaluation. All GPU-hour figures are my rough estimates assuming about 300 tokens per abstract, not measurements.
categories.summary: The finder was mostly reliable. All 19 repos exist, and every metadata field (params, created, license, gated, downloads) matched the live API. Most card numbers matched their sources exactly. Main corrections: (1) STM-Phi4: the numbers came from arXiv v1. The current v3 (Sep 2026, EMNLP Findings) gives STM-Phi4 0.659, not 0.677, roughly tied with E5-large-v2 at 0.654. The released checkpoint is DARE-TIES-merged, not linearly merged, and the '100K beats 1.4M' claim is gone from v3. (2) ChEmbed: the 'nDCG@10 0.82 to 0.91' figure is from the v1 abstract. v2 gives MRR@10 0.781 to 0.882, and it compares against Qwen3-Embedding-8B (0.846), which contradicts the finder's note that no bio model compares against Qwen3-Embedding. (3) MedTE: the paper names this exact repo as its released checkpoint, so that doubt is resolved. (4) nemotron-medical has the same weights as its base for retrieval, so it drops to low; the real candidates are nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B-BF16 and the newer Nemotron-3.5-Embed-8B-BF16. The plain 'nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-8B' repo does not exist. (5) BioELX is dropped as not relevant. Smaller fixes: SPECTER2's own card numbers and its adapter advice; hash-nano is about 7,800x smaller than Qwen3-Embedding-8B, not 1,000x. Priorities: BioHiCL stays high because BiCA-base is built on gte-base, so BioHiCL-Base is the first clean same-backbone (bge-base) control for the gene-disease fine-tune. Scratch files are in /tmp/hfsurvey/verify_bio/.

categories.landscape: I searched the Hub's text-ranking pipeline tag sorted by downloads, created_at, trending and likes (top 1,000 newest), 'reranker' by downloads, about 30 org pages and about 40 keyword searches covering bio and medical terms, MedCPT, BioASQ and reasoning or listwise names (rank1, ReasonRank, Rank-R1, ERank, TFRank, RankZephyr, LiT5, setwise, GroupRank). Cards and papers were read live. From mid-2025 to Nov 2026 the trend is clear. Open rerankers are now mostly Qwen3- or Qwen3.5-based LLM scorers (zerank-2, jina-reranker-v3.5 listwise, Prism, LightOn, KaLM-R2 encoder-decoder, Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B, Oct 2026). At the bottom end, small ModernBERT/Ettin cross-encoders distilled from LLM rerankers (ettin-reranker-v1, May 2026) now beat bge-reranker-v2-m3 on MTEB at 68-150M parameters and run on CPU. Reasoning rerankers (ReasonRank, ERank, GroupRank, Rank-R1/K; Re3Rank published 2026-11-02 with near-zero downloads) carry the only R2MED/BRIGHT-Biology numbers. On R2MED, many of them barely beat a strong retriever (ReasonRank-7B 42.8 vs retriever 42.9). The most useful single finding is a Dictyostelium gene-literature benchmark (arXiv 2610.03130): bge-reranker-v2-gemma reached 0.707 MRR@10 vs MedCPT-CE 0.650, and RankZephyr and MiniLM hurt. That makes bge-reranker-v2-gemma the first thing to try against the Gemini Flash-Lite rerank and as a fine-tuning base. The cheapest test is ettin-reranker-150m fine-tuned against the fine-tuned MedCPT-CE. I looked for and did not find: any MedCPT successor (the ncbi org has none), any BioASQ/TREC-trained open reranker, a Qwen3.5/3.6 reranker from Qwen itself, a bge-reranker-v3, or a new Mixedbread reranker after v2. Biomedical rerankers remain a gap: NeuML biomedbert-base-reranker has no ranking benchmark and tomaarsen's MIRIAD PubMedBERT reranker is weak (NanoBEIR 0.33). Several popular new repos are off-target: tencent R3-rerank (agent skills), Contrastive-LM CLM-v0.1-8B (agent verifier, 790 likes), hs-rerank-1 (memory), Alibaba core-reranker (image compositional). Caveats: zerank-2's vendor claim to beat Gemini 2.5 Flash on biomedical (0.72 vs 0.54) conflicts with an independent MTEB run (0.53, below bge-reranker-v2-m3). Many headline numbers (bge-gemma family, ContextualAI) are only in images, and all cost estimates above are mine, not measured.

categories.summary: I re-checked all 16 candidates live. The finder was reliable: every repo exists, every metadata field matched exactly, and almost every quoted number was found verbatim at its cited source. I dropped none. The main correction: the finder said the bge-gemma BEIR/MIRACL numbers exist only in images, but the bge-reranker-v2.5-gemma2-lightweight card has full text tables. They put v2.5 at BEIR 63.67 and v2-gemma at 60.71, vs 55.36 for v2-m3, and v2.5 wins 3 of 4 bio subsets, so I raised v2.5 to medium. Other fixes: (1) GroupRank-7B's card says 46.8 on R2MED but its paper says 47.8, it ties Rank-R1-7B there, and it trained on Biology/Medical queries with BRIGHT listed, so its BRIGHT-Bio lead is not clean; its paper does show it roughly matching Gemini-2.5-Flash listwise on BRIGHT-Bio (56.85 vs 56.6). (2) The ettin NanoBEIR scores used always_rerank_positives=true, so they are optimistic. (3) gte-reranker-modernbert-base scores below its own sibling embedder on all four bio BEIR subsets, and its card states two different BEIR averages. (4) I lowered mxbai-rerank-large-v2 to low, since ettin-1b matches it and the already-tested Qwen3-Reranker-4B beats it. The two high priorities stand: bge-reranker-v2-gemma (the Dictyostelium numbers are verified, but they come from claim queries, a top-1,000 pool and zero-shot MedCPT) and ettin-150m as a cheap fine-tune base.

categories.landscape:
**The big trend: one backbone, three architectures.** ModernBERT-base (~149M) now carries all three non-dense-or-cheap families. LightOn released DenseOn and LateOn in March 2026 with open training data. Linkup's SPARSEUP (September 2026) trained a sparse model on the same backbone and data. Together they are a controlled dense / late-interaction / sparse trio, the most direct way to ask why BM25 comes so close on the haystack. DenseOn is dense and outside this category, but you need it for that comparison. UIBK-Embedding-v1 (October 2026) puts a dense score and ColBERT token matching into one PLAID index.

**Other trends.** Learned sparse has split into inference-free document-only models (OpenSearch v3; naver's V-SPLADE, which is for visual documents only) and LLM-scale sparse (LACONIC 1B-8B, January 2026; naver splade-code, which is for code). sentence-transformers v5/v6 now loads sparse (SparseEncoder) and multi-vector (MultiVectorEncoder) models, so all three families run in one library. The static side has gone quiet: no new English general or retrieval potion model since early 2025, only code and ONNX variants. NeuML is the only group shipping PubMed-specific sparse, ColBERT, static and tiny models, and it evaluates them only on PubMed title-abstract similarity, never on retrieval.

**What I searched.** HF API by term (splade, neural-sparse, colbert, static, potion, tokenlearn, luxical, minicoil, laconic, plus med/bio/pubmed/clinical combinations). The sparse-encoder, PyLate and model2vec tags, sorted by downloads, created date, trending and likes. Org pages for naver, opensearch-project, lightonai, minishlab, NeuML, mixedbread-ai, jinaai, answerdotai, ibm-granite, sentence-transformers and sparse-encoder. MedEmbed derivatives. The MTEB results repo, which has R2MED Biology for UIBK only. HF papers and the web.

**What I did not find.**
- No sparse or ColBERT model trained on PubMed search logs or gene-disease relevance (nothing like a sparse MedCPT).
- No biomedical learned-sparse model with BioASQ, TREC or R2MED numbers.
- No OpenSearch v4, no IBM r2 sparse model and no Elastic ELSER on HF.
- No jina-colbert-v3 or answerai-colbert v2.

**Excluded, and why.**
- Superseded by LateOn on LateOn's own BEIR table: ColBERT-Zero, GTE-ModernColBERT, jina-colbert-v2, answerai-colbert-small and ColBERTv2.
- Multilingual: LFM2.5-ColBERT (English NanoBEIR 0.687 vs LateOn 0.690 in Liquid's own table; LFM licence) and MILCO.
- Off-task: V-SPLADE (visual documents) and splade-code (code).
- Luxical-One: fast on CPU but uses a web 5-gram vocabulary and reports no benchmarks.

**Two cheap ideas that are not new models.** bge-m3, already covered, also emits sparse and ColBERT outputs, so you can get all three heads from a model you have already run. "Latent Terms" (arXiv 2605.29384) extracts a BM25-ready vocabulary from a frozen dense retriever with a sparse autoencoder; it bears directly on the BM25 question.

**A correction.** Your own RESULTS.md shows the best embedders beating BM25 by +0.06-0.09 recall@10 on the haystack. So the open question is why BM25 comes so close, not why it wins outright. The cost estimates above are rough analogies to your measured ~1.5 L4-h (MedEmbed-base) and ~10 L4-h (Qwen3-E-0.6B) on the 1.7M documents. Scratch files are in /tmp/hfsurvey/sparse/.

categories.summary: The finder was reliable on facts. Every repo exists, every metadata field matched the live API, and every benchmark number I re-checked matched its source (cards, the MTEB results repo, the Linkup blog, the LACONIC paper). That includes SPARSEUP's LACONIC-1B 58.7, which I recomputed from the paper's table. The errors were in cost and relevance framing. (1) genesearch's full 35M MedEmbed index already exists (26 GB float16, GPU-built) and its BM25 is built per gene with bm25s, so the 'cheaper CPU floor / drop-in sparse leg' arguments for Thread B are weak. (2) The CPU-time estimates for BERT-base sparse models are optimistic by about 3-5x against genesearch's measured 50-130 papers/s, and granite-30m-sparse is not cheaper per token than MedEmbed-small. (3) The UIBK and Reason-ModernColBERT 'slots into the suite' claims ignore that the suite uses R2MEDBiologyPooled and llm-eval subsets. (4) The NeuML bio models lowercase their input, which undercuts the Thread D symbol idea. (5) The MedEmbed ONNX repo documents mean pooling where MedEmbed uses CLS pooling, so it is dropped (and it is the already-covered model anyway). Priority changes: OpenSearch v3 and PubMedBERT-SPLADE high -> medium; granite sparse, biomedbert-small and biomedbert-colbert medium -> low. LACONIC's headline repo is switched to the affordable 1B (~$12-15 for 1.7M, code at github.com/zhichaoxu-shufe/laconic-sparse-retrieval). The two highs left are SPARSEUP and LateOn, run with lightonai/DenseOn as a controlled trio. Note that eval/haystack.py is dense-only, so every sparse or ColBERT candidate needs a new scoring path first. Scratch files are in /tmp/hfsurvey/sparse_verify/.

categories.landscape:
I searched the Hub (by downloads, created_at, likes and trending; pipeline tags fill-mask, sentence-similarity and feature-extraction), the author pages (dmis-lab, almanach, NeuML, thomas-sounack, jhu-clsp, LiquidAI, ibm-granite, ncbi, microsoft, bisectgroup, BMRetriever), HF papers, the web and the BLURB leaderboard.

**General-purpose bases:** these moved fastest. UltraBERT (DMIS lab, 2026-10, 32K context) and LFM2.5-Encoder (2026-07) now beat ModernBERT, Ettin and NeoBERT on BEIR after the same fine-tuning sweep. UltraBERT-Embed-150M claims the top MTEB(eng,v2) score under 200M params (67.24 vs bge-base 65.14).

**Biomedical bases:** these moved less. BioClinical-ModernBERT (2025), ModernBERT-bio (almanach, 2026-03, CLM-detour recipe) and MrBERT-biomed (2025-12) are all ModernBERT continuations. They help long and clinical tasks, but on short PubMed tasks PubMedBERT still wins the BigBIO average (80.1 vs 78.9 base / 79.8 large, per the ModernBERT-bio card). BLURB's top is unchanged: BioLinkBERT-Large at 84.30.

**NeuML biomedbert family (2025-12 to 2026-04):** small and base embedders, plus a reranker and a ColBERT, all distilled from a PubMed cross-encoder. These are the newest PubMed-specific fine-tuning starts.

**Recipe caveat:** the thread-A recipe is about 15.7K rows for one epoch. That is too little to turn a raw MLM into a good embedder. So the fair 'which base gains more' sweep is among already-contrastive embedders: UltraBERT-Embed-150M, gte-modernbert-base, NeuML biomedbert-base, and BioClinical-ModernBERT embeddings, at about $0.3 each. Raw MLMs (UltraBERT, ModernBERT-bio, BioClinical-ModernBERT) need a PubMed title-abstract warm-up first. EMBO/ModernBERT-neg-sampling-PubMed is such a warm-up: 26M PMC pairs, no eval published. Raw MLMs fit better as cross-encoder (C8) or NER (thread D) bases.

**Not found:**
- No PubMed-continued UltraBERT, Ettin or LFM2.5.
- No biomedical encoder with published retrieval-after-fine-tuning comparisons. The BioClinical-ModernBERT paper has no retrieval evaluation.
- No PubMed-specific encoder with 32K context.
- No successors to BioLinkBERT or BioM-ELECTRA.
- gyorilab/pubmed_modernbert (2026-07) exists but has an empty card and 0 downloads.
- SciBERT successors (MrBERT-science, SciBETO, SciLaD) are low-download and have no bio evidence.

**Checked but not ranked:**
- Multilingual options (mmBERT-base, EuroBERT, nomic-embed-text-v2-moe with BEIR 52.86, arctic-embed-m-v2.0 with BEIR 55.4) bring nothing for English biology.
- NeoBERT trails (BEIR 42.9, MLDR 21.7 in the UltraBERT table).
- modernbert-embed-base (MTEB eng v2 62.1) is weaker than gte-modernbert-base.

categories.summary: The finder was reliable. All 17 repos exist and every metadata field (params, created, license, gated, downloads) matched the live API exactly. Every headline number was found at its cited source, and the UltraBERT-Embed scores also appear in the official MTEB results repo. Factual fixes were small: the LFM2.5-Encoder card does give a CPU speed figure (3.3x ModernBERT-base at 8K), contrary to the finder; the UltraBERT 'lower LR' warning is on the base card, not the Embed card, and the project's recipe already uses lr 2e-5; the PMC full-text and no-retrieval claims for BioClinical-ModernBERT were checked against the paper. The main corrections are priorities. NeuML biomedbert-base-embeddings drops from high to medium: the covered pubmedbert-base-embeddings gives the same domain arm, and its edge is a +1.25 in-domain self-eval. NeuML bioclinical-modernbert embeddings, ModernBERT-bio, BioClinical-ModernBERT and granite-small-r2 drop from medium to low: PubMedBERT still wins short-abstract gene/disease NER, and neither 8K context nor general small embedders answer an open question here. Only UltraBERT-Embed-150M stays high, as a sub-$1 test of 'does a better base gain more'.

categories.landscape:
I searched the Hub by name (medgemma, txgemma, Baichuan-M, II-Medical, OpenBioLLM, BioMistral, meditron, HuatuoGPT, MedReason, m1, Intern-S1, AlphaMed, judge, rerank, plus medical/bio/clinical/pubmed/gene terms), sorted by downloads, created_at, trending and likes. I also scanned the recent releases of about 30 orgs (google, Qwen, openai, microsoft, meta-llama, meta-models, mistralai, allenai, HuggingFaceTB, nvidia, ibm-granite, deepseek-ai, zai-org, moonshotai, MiniMaxAI, FreedomIntelligence, baichuan-inc, EPFLiGHT, UCSC-VLAA, ZJU-AI4H and others), pulled live per-token prices from router.huggingface.co/v1/models, and read cards and papers.

The 2026 trend is sparse MoE with 3-6B active parameters and 256K-1M context: Gemma 4 26B-A4B, gpt-oss, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (6B active), Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B. HF providers sell these at $0.03-0.15 per 1M input tokens, against Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite at $0.25 standard / $0.125 batch. So 'cheaper than Flash-Lite' is easy. The open questions are quality and reproducibility, and an open, version-pinned judge helps a paper.

Biomedical LLMs are now thin RL/SFT layers on Qwen or Gemma bases: HuatuoGPT-3 (Qwen3.5/3.8), II-Medical (Qwen3), Baichuan-M3 (Qwen3-235B), MedDecider (Qwen3.5/3.8, Gemma 4), ClinSeek (Qwen3.5), MeditronFO (Gemma 3/OLMo 2/Apertus). They target clinical QA and HealthBench, not literature relevance, and the gains over their bases are small. MeditronFO beats Gemma-3-27B-IT by +0.63 average, and on SciHorizon-GENE gene-function reasoning MedGemma-27B (41.32) trails Gemma 3 27B (47.75).

There is no MedGemma 2 or Gemma-4-based MedGemma (only MedGemma 1.5 4B). TxGemma, OpenBioLLM, BioMistral, m1 and MedReason have no 2026 successors. Meta's open line is now 'Muse' (Glimmer-30B, Spark-Open-816B-A42B), not Llama 5. There is no new Phi LLM or SmolLM4, OLMo 3 is still Ai2's latest general model, and Mistral Small 4 is 119B-A6B, which does not fit an L4.

Cheap open successors of API models you already use exist but are not listed: GLM-5.3-Flash (320B-A18B, MIT, $0.15/$0.50), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ($0.20/$0.60 deepinfra) and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash ($0.15/$0.60). nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B (Oct 2026) belongs to the reranker survey.

I did not find:
- any head-to-head of open LLMs on PubMed or BioASQ document reranking, or on gene-disease relevance judging (CLEF/BioASQ 2026 notes mention LLM top-20 reranks but showed no model/score in what I saw);
- any open model trained specifically as a biomedical relevance judge;
- any medical numbers (MedQA/PubMedQA) on the Qwen3.8 cards.

categories.summary: The finder's metadata was reliable: all 17 repos exist, and params, dates, licenses, gating, downloads, router prices and provider lists matched the live data. Most card numbers checked out exactly too. The main errors were in interpretation and sourcing. The SciHorizon-GENE MedGemma-vs-Gemma-3 gap is not like-for-like: Gemma 3 has no Gene Ontology score, so the matched averages are 44.90 vs 47.75, not 41.32 vs 47.75. The OnePO paper (arXiv 2610.05966) does compare HuatuoGPT-3 with its bases and shows large gains (HealthBench Professional 68.3 vs 31.9 for the 9B), which contradicts the finder's 'no base comparison' and 'small gains'. The Flash-Next bio numbers come from the Fx-Bio 0913 card, not 1031; Evidence Inference and BioNLI training belongs to MedDecider-27B, not 4B; Baichuan-M3 INT4 is 124.5 GB (not a single 80 GB GPU); and the Qwen3.8-27B AWQ quant is 21 GB, so it barely fits an L4. On priorities: the repo already runs a cheap open-weight rerank (BM25 + DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 0.832 for $0.13), so the real open question is a rerank or judge free of judge self-preference. That keeps gpt-oss-120b high, moves Gemma 4 26B-A4B to medium (Google lineage) and MedDecider-4B to low, and drops Fx-Bio. Two items the finder missed, for the report: google/gemma-4-12B-it (apache-2.0, 12.0B, 1.77M downloads, no providers; on the card, MRCR 128k 43.4 vs 44.1 for the 26B-A4B) and lion-ai/MedDecider-4B-NLI (a standard sequence-classification export that runs on CPU).

categories.landscape: Searched with the hf CLI and API (downloads, created_at and trending sorts) for hunflair, gliner-bio/biomed, OpenMed NER and ZeroShot, sapbert, krissbert, biosyn, aioner, gnorm, bern2, pubtator, nlm-gene, gnormplus, bc2gm, bc5cdr, biored, medmentions, umls, hgnc, abbreviation/acronym, UniNER and entity-linking. I also checked org pages (ncbi, lingbionlp, dmis-lab, OpenMed, knowledgator, Ihor, Glasgow-AI4BioMed, ElucidataInc, Dash00), HF papers search, and the HunFlair2 (2402.12372), PubTator3 (2401.11048) and BeLink (2605.22501) papers. Most gene NER on the Hub is still 2022-2025 BERT taggers (BC2GM/JNLPBA) plus OpenMed's large family, whose near-identical ~90k-200k download counts look automated. The 2025-26 activity is in GLiNER-style zero-shot taggers (GLiNER-biomed, GLiNER2.5, GLiFormer) and in LLM-based linking. BeLink (SIGIR'26) puts unofficial, cardless Qwen3-8B set-wise reranker checkpoints on HF, and its paper reports NLM-Gene Acc@1 51.6 vs 27.3 for SapBERT retrieval. PubTator3's own pieces (AIONER, GNorm2) exist only as a zip and a third-party Docker mirror. Caveat for scoring: NLM-Gene is in the training data of AIONER (PubTator3), HunFlair2 and the BeLink nlm-gene reranker, so only the NLM-Gene test split is fair, and PubTator3 is in-domain there. Its BioRED gene F is 84.63 and its tmVar v3 gene F1 is 86.02 vs HunFlair2's 76.75, so expect PubTator to win on average and disagree on the long tail. I found no HF model built for the exact question 'is this bare short symbol (SE/AST/TNM/CAR/ACE/PC/Fe) a gene here?'. The closest tools are context-aware taggers (HunFlair2), zero-shot competing-label taggers (GLiNER-biomed), a Gene vs FamilyName tagger (Glasgow GNormPlus model, for the 'cathepsins' problem), and linkers that can return NIL. An LLM judge already in use (e.g. Gemini Flash-Lite) remains a strong option outside this category. Also checked and not reported: UniNER-7B (2023, CC-BY-NC), GLiNKER/gliner-linker (general Wikidata linking, no bio numbers), Ihor/gliner-*-v2.5-biomed (Feb 2026, no card, 0 downloads), BioELX retriever (cross-lingual UMLS), NA-SapBERT (clinical), Elucidata polly-ner (BC2GM F1 0.833, another BC2GM tagger), dmis-lab UltraBERT (Oct 2026, general-domain encoder, no bio NER numbers), ncbi/Gene-R1 (gene-set analysis, not NER). Datasets for calibration are on the Hub: bigbio/nlm_gene and bigbio/gnormplus."

candidates.name: HunFlair2 NER
candidates.kind: NER (gene, disease, chemical, species; Flair prefixed tagger)
candidates.params: unknown (no safetensors; single 434 MB pytorch_model.bin, about base size)
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2402.12372 Table 3, cross-corpus mention-level micro F1 for end-to-end NER+NEN. Gene on tmVar v3: PubTator 86.02, HunFlair2 76.75, BERN2 43.96, bent 0.54. Average over 4 entity types: HunFlair2 58.79, PubTator 54.33. Gene training corpora include NLM-Gene and GNormPlus. The paper does not say whether the NLM-Gene test split was held out of training.
candidates.relevance: Thread D: an independent, context-aware second-opinion gene tagger. Run it on abstracts where PubTator3 tagged a bare short symbol (SE, AST, TNM, CAR, ACE, PC, Fe) and count where HunFlair2 tags no gene, giving an error-candidate rate per symbol. It learned from the same corpora as PubTator3 (NLM-Gene, GNormPlus), so the two are not fully independent and may share label conventions.
candidates.cost_to_try: CPU is fine for targeted subsets. Needs flair>=0.14 and scispacy; no trust_remote_code. Running all 7.76M abstracts would be a GPU job (not measured).
candidates.verify_note: Live metadata matches: created 2024-02-14, 2,371 downloads, no license, no safetensors (434 MB .bin). Every Table 3 number was found in the arXiv HTML. Correction: the finder said 'only the NLM-Gene test split is clean'. That is unverified for HunFlair2. The paper lists NLM-Gene among its 8 training corpora and never says the test split was held out. Its cross-corpus protocol gave it no reason to hold the split out. flair's HUNER_GENE_NLM_GENE loader uses the BigBio splits, but training may have folded the test split in. So treat NLM-Gene test as possibly contaminated for HunFlair2. Kept at high because it is a cheap CPU run aimed squarely at the open thread-D question. Added a caveat about shared training corpora.

candidates.name: BiomedBERT GNormPlus tagger (Gene / FamilyName / DomainMotif)
candidates.kind: NER (token classification)
candidates.evidence: Model card, GNormPlus test, span-level: Gene P 0.856 / R 0.923 / F1 0.888; FamilyName P 0.497 / R 0.569 / F1 0.530; DomainMotif F1 0.634.
candidates.relevance: Thread D, family-plural errors: flag PubTator3 gene mentions that this model labels FamilyName (e.g. 'cathepsins'), then spot-check them. FamilyName precision is about 0.50, so half the flags will be wrong. It is trained on the GNormPlus corpus, whose FamilyName class GNorm2 also learns from, so it is not an independent referee. A simple plural/regex rule may do about as well.
candidates.cost_to_try: Plain transformers pipeline on CPU; minutes for tens of thousands of abstracts.
candidates.verify_note: Metadata matches (108,897,031 params, MIT, 9 downloads, created 2025-07-09). All card numbers confirmed. Corrections: (1) The finder called it 'the only off-the-shelf HF model that tags families'. That is false: the finder's own OpenMed ZeroShot Protein candidate has a protein_family_or_group label. (2) The tokenizer is uncased (do_lower_case=True), so it cannot use case cues such as CAR vs car. (3) It is trained on the same corpus and guidelines as PubTator3's GNorm2, so it is not independent. Priority lowered from high to medium: FamilyName precision is 0.497, and a rule baseline is untested.

candidates.name: HunFlair gene linker (BioSyn-SapBERT BC2GN + human NCBI Gene)
candidates.kind: entity linker (gene normalisation to human NCBI Gene; context-free)
candidates.params: unknown (no safetensors; 5.43 GB .bin including precomputed human gene_info dictionary embeddings)
candidates.dims_or_context: 768-d mention-string embeddings; nearest neighbour over Homo_sapiens.gene_info
candidates.evidence: No standalone number on the card. Inside the HunFlair2 pipeline, gene NER+NEN on tmVar v3 scores F1 76.75 (arXiv 2402.12372 Table 3). The paper says the linker covers only the human subset of NCBI Gene and 'does not use context information for linking, it cannot effectively handle intra-species gene ambiguity' (its example is TPO).
candidates.relevance: Thread D: a second gene-ID assignment to compare with PubTator3/GNorm2 IDs. It ignores context, so the same string always gets the same ID. It therefore cannot settle context-dependent ambiguity (ACE vs ACE2, CAR as NR1I3 vs a cell therapy); any disagreement is a string-level artefact, not evidence about the abstract.
candidates.cost_to_try: CPU-feasible. 5.4 GB download, or rebuild it from dmis-lab/biosyn-sapbert-bc2gn with EntityMentionLinker.build (shown on the card). Needs flair.
candidates.verify_note: Metadata matches (created 2024-01-29, 113 downloads, 5,433,808,687-byte .bin, no license). The card confirms the dictionary is Homo_sapiens.gene_info. Corrected the relevance: the finder used 'disagreement on ID for ACE/CAR' as an error signal, but the HunFlair2 paper says this linker ignores context and cannot resolve within-species ambiguity. Priority lowered from medium to low.

candidates.name: GLiNER-BioMed large
candidates.kind: zero-shot span NER (GLiNER uni-encoder, DeBERTa-v3-large, cased)
candidates.dims_or_context: labels given at inference (max_types 30); gliner_config max_len 2048 words, max span width 12

candidates.verify_note: Metadata matches (created 2025-02-19, 1,515 downloads, apache-2.0, no safetensors). Benchmark numbers confirmed on the card and in the paper. Corrections: the context is max_len 2048 per gliner_config, not about 512. The 59.77 is micro F1 over 8 mostly clinical datasets, and only BioRED has genes. Medium is defensible: CPU-cheap, and it targets the symbol-type question directly, but it is unvalidated on genes.

candidates.name: BeLink reranker (NLM-Gene) 8B
candidates.kind: LLM reranker for entity linking (set-wise, fine-tuned from Qwen3-8B-Base)
candidates.dims_or_context: chooses among the top-20 aliases from SapBERT retrieval over NCBI Gene (all species), plus a 'None of the above' option
candidates.license: not stated on HF (no model card); GitHub code dash-ka/BeLink is MIT
candidates.evidence: arXiv 2605.22501 (SIGIR'26) Table 1, NLM-Gene Acc@1 / NIL-sensitive Acc@1: first-stage retrieval baseline 27.3; GPT-4o-as-reranker 47.0/47.0; Qwen3-reranker-8B 49.9/43.8; BeLink-reranker-8B 51.6/49.9; BeLink-reranker-4B 47.6/47.5. GNormPlus: BeLink-8B 81.5/79.9. Speed 16.5 Q/s vs 4.3 for Qwen3-reranker-8B. The first stage is SapBERT retrieval after Qwen3-14B query reformulation (GenQR). Per the GitHub README, the test set drops mentions that exactly overlap train+val mentions, so these scores are not on the standard NLM-Gene test split.
candidates.relevance: Thread D, normalisation only. Given a span plus its sentence, it picks an NCBI Gene ID or 'None of the above'. The NIL option means 'correct gene not among the candidates', and training saw only true gene mentions. So it does not answer 'is this span a gene at all' (SE/AST/TNM), which is the main thread-D question. It could re-check PubTator3 IDs for ambiguous genes. The LLM judge already in use covers the gene-or-not question more cheaply.
candidates.cost_to_try: GPU: 8B in bf16 fits an L4. The repo also holds a 32.8 GB optimizer.pt, so download only the *.safetensors and tokenizer files. The full pipeline also needs a SapBERT alias index and optionally Qwen3-14B GenQR. There is no card, so the prompt comes from the dash-ka/BeLink code. CPU route: mradermacher GGUF quants of the sibling QLink-nlm-gene-8B and -4B exist; the source of the 4B is no longer public (401).
candidates.verify_note: Metadata matches (8,190,735,360 params, created 2026-01-31, 6 downloads, no license, Qwen3ForCausalLM config). Every Table 1 number cited was found in the arXiv HTML. Corrections: (1) The 27.3 baseline is SapBERT retrieval after Qwen3-14B GenQR over a multi-species NCBI Gene KB, not plain SapBERT. (2) The test set is filtered to unseen mentions (GitHub README), so it is not comparable to standard NLM-Gene test scores. (3) The NIL option is not a 'not a gene' detector. (4) The repo carries a 32.8 GB optimizer.pt. Priority lowered from medium to low: it does not address the gene-or-not question and needs a GPU plus pipeline reconstruction.

categories.summary: The finder was reliable on facts. Live metadata matched for all 17 repos (params, dates, licences, downloads), and every headline number turned up at its cited source (HunFlair2 Table 3, PubTator3 Supp. Table 3, BeLink Table 1, all model cards). The main corrections are about interpretation and priority. (1) The claim that the NLM-Gene test split is clean is unverified for HunFlair2. It is probably false for PubTator3 itself: GNorm2 ships 'Allset' models trained on all datasets, so PubTator3 calibration on NLM-Gene test may be optimistic. (2) BeLink's 27.3 baseline is SapBERT after Qwen3-14B query reformulation over a multi-species KB and a filtered test set, and its NIL option does not detect non-genes. (3) The HunFlair linker and SapBERT ignore context, so they cannot settle ACE/CAR-type ambiguity. (4) Glasgow MedMentions emits 14 groups, not 21 types. (5) GLiNER-biomed context is 2048, not 512. Priorities lowered: Glasgow GNormPlus high to medium (uncased, FamilyName precision 0.50, same corpus as GNorm2); BeLink, SapBERT and the biosyn linker medium to low. Dropped: BERN2 (stale 2021, custom arch, GNormPlus lineage) and GLiNER2.5-Disease (off-target). Only HunFlair2 stays high.

categories.summary: The finder returned only 3 real candidates plus an empty placeholder (dropped), short of the 8-15 asked for. All 3 are precomputed gene-embedding datasets, not models. That is a sensible choice for CPU-only gene-level work, but none of the model families in the brief (Geneformer, ESM C, TranscriptFormer and others) got its own entry. Live metadata was accurate on all three, and every benchmark number the finder cited checked out. Main corrections: BoevaLab's cited GitHub repo is 404 (the live repo is DanielTabaresLopez/Gene-Embeddings), and its PrimeKG and Hetionet vectors are TF-IDF+SVD, not TransE. GenePT Revisited was an ICLR 2026 MLGenX workshop poster, not a main-conference paper, and its 'uniprot' file is probably ProtT5, not UniProt text. The GenBio dataset does carry a non-commercial license, contrary to the finder's 'not stated'. Priorities were lowered: BoevaLab from high to medium (cheap and the best fit, but the open D task can be done directly from the gene2pubtator3 mention text) and GenePT Revisited from medium to low.

categories.landscape: Searches covered: Hub model search by downloads and by creation date (trending sort returned nothing useful); tags (biology, single-cell, protein, genomics, scRNA-seq, gene-expression); org pages (biohub, arcinstitute, genbio-ai, vandijklab, InstaDeepAI, westlake-repl, Rostlab, theislab, Bitbol-Lab, mims-harvard, tahoebio, Synthyra, perturblab, ncbi, zjunlp, NeuML); HF dataset search; HF papers; web search. Every repo above was checked live. The biggest finding is not a model: BoevaLab/Gene-Embedding-Hub-dataset (already found) holds 68 gene matrices aligned to 20,097 protein-coding genes. These cover ESM2, ProtT5/PROBE, Geneformer V2-316M, scGPT, UCE, scFoundation, scPRINT, GenePT, BioConceptVec, PrimeKG/Hetionet context, STRING (Mashup, deepNF), GO, DepMap, GTEx, Mahi, NT-v2/DNABERT-2 CDS, and AlphaGenome/Enformer TSS. So the C/E/D question (does literature geometry match sequence, expression and knowledge geometry?) can be answered first at zero compute. Most models here only matter for axes the hub lacks. Those are: ESMC-6B (biohub, May 2026; MIT-licensed; 300M/600M/6B plus SAEs and ESMFold2), PROTON's learned KG embeddings, ProteomeLM's proteome-context vectors, and ProTrek's shared protein-text space, which gives D a per-(paper, gene) plausibility score. Prior work to cite: PRISME (arXiv 2507.07367) used an adjusted SVCCA and found that omics, literature-text and KG gene embeddings carry largely non-overlapping signal. Kan-Tor et al. 2024 (arXiv 2412.04075) found text models best on genomic and regulatory tasks, expression models best on localization and process, and protein models best on protein properties; I saw no per-model numbers. Searched for and not found on HF: TranscriptFormer (CZI ships it via pip and S3), official scGPT (only ports), TxGNN, Hetionet/BioKG embedding models, ProtLLM, an ESM3-large or ESM4 open release (only esm3-sm-open-v1), and a CellFM by that name (BoHuangLab/CELL-FM is a microscopy model; real CellFM is only at perturblab). genbio-ai/STRING_GNN exists but is empty, and genbio-ai renamed AIDO.* to GB.*. UCE's gene tokens are frozen ESM2, so it adds nothing over ESM2. ProteinDT, BioBridge (yuccaaa) and ProtST repos have near-zero downloads and no gene-level use. Evolla, Pinal, Prot2Text-V2, BioT5 and ncbi/Gene-R1 generate text and have no per-gene vector. Few gene-level models publish benchmark numbers on their cards; the ones I saw are PROTON's link-prediction AUROC and ProteomeLM-ess's essentiality AUROCs.
categories.summary:
The finder was reliable on facts. I re-ran the live metadata call for all 21 model repos and 2 datasets. Every params, created, license, gated and downloads value matched, and no repo was missing or renamed. One exception: Tahoe-x1's safetensors total is the 3B variant at the repo root, not a sum across the repo. The main corrections are judgement calls:
- ESMC-6B is cut from high to medium. The finder's own plan runs the free ESM2 hub vectors first, so ESMC-6B is a follow-up, not a cheap answer to an open question.
- Geneformer and SapBERT drop to low. The Geneformer axis is already free in the BoevaLab hub, and a plain UMLS/MeSH string count does SapBERT's core job without a model.
- Four are dropped. SE-600M's gene table is ESM2: its config.yaml points to gene_symbol_to_embedding_ESM2.pt. The perturblab scELMo pickle is GenePT-ada, which the hub already has. C2S-Scale has no gene vector, and Evo 2 has no realistic gene-level output.
- Smaller fixes. ProTrek's evidence was 'none'; its bioRxiv abstract has numbers, now added. A paraphrase of Kan-Tor was tightened. The claim that official scGPT is not on HF is not quite right: wanglab/scGPT-human holds a copy in the original format but has no model card.

The bioRxiv abstract (Candido et al. 2026, 'Language Modeling Materializes a World Model of Protein Biology') gives no ESMC numbers either. Facts the card does give: 80 layers, 2.37e23 training FLOPs, and ESMFold2 is trained on a frozen ESMC-6B.

One vector per gene: mean-pool the final layer over the canonical UniProt isoform, then map UniProt to HGNC/Entrez. The vector encodes sequence, evolution and fold, not literature. Experiment: per-gene literature centroids (mean MedEmbed vector over each gene's papers) vs this axis, compared by kNN overlap and CKA. D: genes whose literature neighbours ignore their paralogue family are mis-tag candidates.
candidates.cost_to_try: My estimate is 1-2 L4 GPU-hours for about 20k canonical proteins (roughly 2 x 6.35e9 x 11M residues = 1.4e17 FLOPs). Weights are stored in fp32 (6 shards, about 25.4 GB to download); loaded in bf16 they take about 12.7 GB, which fits a 24 GB L4. transformers main has a native 'esmc' model, and the repo also ships modeling_esmc_remote.py via auto_map, so older transformers need trust_remote_code. Proteins over 2048 aa need chunking. ESMC-300M is CPU-feasible in hours.

Priority cut from high to medium. The finder's own plan is to run the free hub ESM2 vectors first and switch to ESMC-6B only if the sequence axis shows signal, so this is a follow-up, not a cheap answer to an open question. The paper's 'one large modern model to add' means a text embedder for 7.76M abstracts, not a protein LM. Added notes: the weights download in fp32 (about 25 GB), and auto_map / trust_remote_code applies on older transformers. Side finding: the EvolutionaryScale org now redirects to biohub. The 2024 weights live at biohub/esmc-300m-2024-12 and biohub/esmc-600m-2024-12 (.pth files). gaps.landscape:
I checked successors of covered families live: Qwen, BAAI, jina, Alibaba-NLP, nomic, Snowflake, granite, mixedbread, e5, ncbi, NeuML, FremyCompany, MedEmbed, BMRetriever, BiCA, MedCPT. I also scanned 2025-10 to 2026-11 sentence-similarity, feature-extraction and text-ranking releases by likes and downloads, plus biomedical keyword sweeps, HF papers, and the R2MED leaderboard.

The biggest gap was reasoning-intensive retrieval for the R2MED biology slot. The R2MED leader is the ReasonEmbed 0928 checkpoint, not the listed 0923 one. ReasonRank and NVIDIA's reasoning embedder were also missing. The R2MED leaderboard also shows LLM query rewriting is huge on Biology (o3-mini + BM25 59.65 vs BM25 19.19), which argues for testing Gemini-based query expansion before HF doc2query models.

A large Sep-Oct 2026 trend is 'System One' typed-decision models (JEV, Laya, OpenJev, CLM, MetaEncoder). They are relevant only as one-pass relevance judges; none has retrieval or biomedical evidence.

Independent support for the listed bge-reranker-v2-gemma: a 2026 dictyBase curation benchmark (arXiv 2610.03130) found it the best reranker (MRR@10 0.707 vs MedCPT-CE 0.650, bge-reranker-v2-m3 0.605, BM25 0.593). The same benchmark found gene-synonym query expansion helps weaker rerankers.

Searched with nothing worth adding:
- MeSH indexing: only undocumented 0-download GRPO Qwen3 indexers (josh-oo) and French-oriented evalLLM2026 MeSH linkers (cea-list).
- Chemistry synonyms: nothing beyond the listed ChEmbed; no ChemTEB update.
- Keyphrase / cluster-labelling: only 2022-era ml6team KBIR/KeyBART and BERTopic demos.
- Claim verification: small student models only.
- Biomedical figure+text: BiomedCLIP 2023, MedSigLIP 2025, open-pmc-18m-clip; no thread uses figures.
- Long-context / contextual chunk embedders: pplx-embed-v2-context 0.6b/9b (Oct 2026) and SciEmbed-ctx-8192; abstracts don't need them.

No new text successor exists for MedCPT, BMRetriever, BiCA, MedEmbed, BioLORD, BGE, E5, nomic, Snowflake or mixedbread. Qwen's only 2026 embedder is the multimodal Qwen3-VL line, which is weaker on text. NCBI's Gene-R1 1B/3B/8B have empty cards. LFM2.5-Embedding-350M was skipped (English NanoBEIR 0.644 vs Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B 0.649). API-only embedders (Gemini, Voyage, Cohere, OpenAI) are outside this Hub survey.
